revisionDesc.change: Vote - AcceptText - Σακβέλιος (ln 1), παντὸς (ln 4), and ψιλὸς τώπος (ln 5) are good. I agree with Sosin that more dotting in line 6 ( ἕτ̣ε̣ροι ψ̣ι̣λ̣οὶ) may be in order; it looks as if damage to the papyrus caused the writer to leave a space between ε and τεροι. The proposed emendation to line 10, Ταορσεῦτι (l. Ταορσεῦτος), is also good.

Vote - AcceptText - Accept. Lin2 Σακβέλιος clearly legible in PSI image online (http://psi-online.it/documents/psi;8;916); lin4 I think παντὸς is also quite clear (more than just the sigma; I see tau omicron well enough too); lin5 ψιλὸς τώπος (l. τόπος) also clear in my view. Lin6 I agree the text must read ἕτεροι ψιλοὶ but I cannot quite see that in the image; I see ε followed by what looks like space for 3 letters (not 2), then ροι (clearly); in the next word I think I can make out -οι, but cannot see ψιλ in the traces preceding. I think the reading ought to be right and would urge retaining, but dotting: ἕτ̣ε̣ροι ψ̣ι̣λ̣οὶ. Lin10 the hand is so shaky that it is hard to tell, but Ταορσεῦτι (l. Ταορσεῦτος) is plausible; the scribe clearly did not write Ταορσεῦτος (note BTW that the scribe very clearly wrote μητρρος in lin10, whether dittography or a failed attempt to go back over the first ρ I don't know)

line 2: Σακχαῖος → Σακβέλιος based on digital image (psi-online), supported by the duplicate P.Mich. V 309.2 line 4: πάντα → παντὸς based on digital image: the sigma is pretty clear, and παντὸς is expected, as in the duplicate, line 3 line 5: Φιλήμονος → ψιλὸς τώπος (l. τόπος) based on digital image, entering also the BL correction 3.226 which had suggested simply → ψιλὸς τόπος line 6: ε̣π̣ικαρουχινοι → ἕτ̣ε̣ροι ψ̣ιλοὶ based on digital image, supported by the duplicate, line 5 line 10: Ταορσεῦτος → Ταορσεῦτι (l. Ταορσεῦτος) based on the digital image: where ed. pr. read -ος it seems clear that there is only a single letter written, and while it is slightly more curved than other iotas in this hand, it is much closer to iota than sigma [I am also proposing correcting the duplicate, line 9, to the same reading; ed. pr. Ταορσεῦτ<ο>ς]
